output.name: Ruhkan — The Frost-Hand
output.myth:
In the hard winter of the long salt, Ruhk made kites for the whole Windward coast. His fingers went white, then black, and three came off at the second knuckle. Ruhk did not sit down about it. He pricked his stumps through the cloth with a bone needle, bound them with gut, and went on stitching. His kites never tore. Not once. Tavo, the Gale, who tears everything, came down the coast and found no seam to pull. He laughed until the cliffs rang, then went looking for a better game.

Mother Hesk saw the hand he held up to the wind and counted it. The Gull Who Flew the String watched from the north-west and carried the news to the Reel. When Ruhk went aloft, Ennu pinned his hand above the north where Hesk could wind it. It is still there, open, holding a kite string that goes down into the dark. Ruskel, the Fid, lies south-east of it, and the sky's frayed ends are knotted there still. Children who fly badly are told to ask Ruhk for steady hands.
output.finding: Find Hirun, the Gull Who Flew the String, and look one hand-span (about 20°) to her south-east, where the open Frost-Hand holds its string above the north.
